messages:
marta: Heads-up — after yesterday's client rollout we're seeing a ~120-300ms stall on initial paint for sparklines and small metric charts. Happens on cold loads.
liam: ugh. any correlation with the bundle change?
marta: yes — stack traces point to main-thread CPU spent in telemetry serialization and the new prefetch heuristic. flame shows main > telemetry.serialize ~35-45% during initial paint.
ryan: deploy-bot just posted canary metrics: p95 for chart paint jumped from 220ms to 480ms in eu-canary. link: https://telemetry/reports/4132 (internal)
deploy-bot: canary eu-1 updated at 2026-03-19T22:03Z, traffic=10% -> p95_chart_paint=480ms (+2.2x)
olivia: ok. likely two things: the telemetry bundler was moved into the main chunk and prefetch now eagerly fetches chart datasets + telemetry flush on same tick.
ben: can we confirm by toggling telemetry bundle out of main? simple repro: locally build with TELEMETRY_IN_WORKER=true and prefetchTTL=20s.
marta: repro confirmed on local with worker telemetry — paint stalls vanish (~+20ms).
liam: so quick mitigation: revert the bundling change OR move telemetry flush off-main (worker). also consider lowering prefetch concurrency for cold route.
ryan: i'm +1 for worker move. moving bundler back to a separate chunk won't fully fix until prefetch timing adjusted, because we still flush large payloads right before first paint.
olivia: small config tweak we tested: set prefetchTTL from 60k -> 15k and reduce telemetry.sampleRate from 1.0 -> 0.25 for canary. improved p95 to ~270ms.
marta: here's the telemetry snippet we used locally:
```
{"sampleRate":0.25,"bundleSizeLimit":45000,"prefetchTTLms":15000,"flushOnNavigate":false}
```
liam: nice. two parallel efforts: 1) short-term canary config change & route throttle 2) medium-term: off-main telemetry worker + ensure bundler chunk is async-loaded after initial render.
ben: i've drafted PR to gate sampleRate by runtime flag and to spawn a worker for the bundler. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/9842 (WIP)
marta: can we also adjust routing policy to prefer warm-kv affinity for chart routes? that would reduce cold prefetches hitting remote region. e.g., route rule: "prefer: kv_affinity=hot then latency"
ryan: yes, ops can flip a routing policy in gateway for canary: set route.kv_prefetch_priority=LOW for 10% traffic.
olivia: i'll run the canary with telemetry.sampleRate=0.25 + prefetchTTL=15000 + route.kv_prefetch_priority=LOW for 2h, monitor chart p95 and main thread % cpu.
telemetry-bot: alert muted for this canary window. threshold check disabled: chart_p95 > 400ms -> notify.
deploy-bot: canary started at 2026-03-20T01:12Z, targets: eu-canary (10%), us-west (5%).
liam: if canary metrics look good after 1h, we can roll config to 50% then schedule PR merge for worker bundler.
ben: note: moving bundler to worker requires changes in build pipeline to emit worker bundle and a small runtime shim:
```js
if (TELEMETRY_IN_WORKER) new Worker('/telemetry.worker.js')
else import('./telemetry-bundle')
```
marta: OK. action items:
• olivia -> run canary with config flags (started)
• ben -> finish PR + tests for worker shim (next 6h)
• liam -> prep rollback steps if canary regresses (ticket #INC-4132)
• ryan -> tweak gateway route for kv_prefetch_priority (done for canary)
Thanks all :thumbsup:
liam: ping me if you need an emergency revert. I'll stand by.
ryan: logging a quick note: add a perf test for main-thread telemetry.serialize to CI (non-flaky) — adding to eng-runtime backlog.
marta: will follow up with a short postmortem after canary. keep threads here.
